title: strictKeyValidation is not validation - it silently rewrites and collides
rationale: The flag reads as a gate. sanitizeKey implements it as a character-class replaceAll, which rejects nothing, reports nothing, and maps a large class of distinct names onto the same output. Three punctuation variants of the same stem is the minimum case that demonstrates the fold and the invented suffixes together.
catchesBugClass: A control whose name promises rejection and whose implementation performs unlogged, order-dependent, information-destroying rewriting. Pins that a correct fix must either reject or return the applied mapping.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch a cross-document collision, because escaping runs after the fold. The injectivity break is confined to within a single object level.

predicted.detail: All three fold to one name and the clashes are resolved with invented numeric suffixes. The folding is defensible for SQL-safe identifiers; emitting no mapping, no warning and no exception is not.
